Should / Ought to / Had Better for Obligation and Recommendation
You use should, ought to and had better to give advice.
There are some points to keep in mind about using these modal verbs.

1. You use either ought to or should to provide advice.
    For example:
    The policy says that the company should reimburse employees for holiday hours.
    You ought to see a doctor as soon as you can.

1. Although should, ought to and had better have the same meaning, ought to implies a negative consequence if you don't follow the advice.
    For example:
    We had better call the police right away!
1. Ought to and had better are not used in questions.

1. In negative sentences, the word not goes after should, and had better but after ought (ought not).
    For example:
    You should not (shouldn't) smoke inside your apartment. (shouldn't is the contraction of should not). You had better not smoke inside the apartment. (there is no contraction when using had better).
    You ought not smoke inside the apartment. (there is no contraction when using ought to and ‘to' is dropped).
The uneven distribution of income and wealth, called income inequality or economic inequality, should be seen as one of the critical challenges of our time.
These people believe that governments ought to have a role in redistributing wealth among citizens within its society.
They think everyone ought to benefit from free market forces.
The study came on the heels of a previous study published one month earlier that said changes ought to be made to environmental policies.
The researchers argue that economic leaders around the world should understand the consequences of global warming.
Once leaders realize the impact of climate change, they ought to act in a concerted way to reduce the risks of increased inequality.
Will and Would to Ask Politely or to Insist
You can use will and would to ask for things politely. You can also use will when you want to insist on doing something.

For example:
Will you come with me, please?
Will you sign on the dotted line, please?
Would you please tell her that her doctor called?
Would you do me a favor, please?
Depending on the context, a request can also function as a command.
When you want to insist on doing something, even if it is not recommended or inadvisable, you can use will.

For example:
If you will refuse to see the dentist, it's no surprise your tooth is getting worse.
In this case, when you say a sentence like this, you need to put strong stress on the word will.
If you will make rich people pay higher taxes, income distribution would be much fairer.
Will you seriously consider decreasing carbon emissions, so there will be beneficial consequences to the world economy?
Would you be so kind as to complete our online survey?
Would you send us a message with your point of view?

images.text:
You know the expression: “The rich get richer while the poor get poorer”. The uneven distribution of income and wealth, called income inequality or economic inequality, should be seen as one of the critical challenges of our time.
Economic inequality is the result of many factors. Some people argue that taxation policies often favor people with a greater income. These people believe that governments ought to have a role in redistributing wealth among citizens within its society. They say, “It's just not fair! If you will make rich people pay higher taxes, income distribution would be much fairer.” Other people point to factors such as greater returns on investment that wealthy people usually enjoy. They think everyone ought to benefit from free market forces.

A new study published by researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, uses science to make a connection between the issues of economic inequality and climate change. The study came on the heels of a previous study published one month earlier that said changes ought to be made to environmental policies. In essence, the study said to world leaders: Will you seriously consider decreasing carbon emissions, so there will be beneficial consequences to the world economy?
The study found that climate change will increase global inequality. Global warming is beneficial for colder countries such as Europe, which tend to be richer and more advanced, but more harmful for poorer countries with warmer temperatures, such as those in Africa and South Asia.

The researchers argue that economic leaders around the world should understand the consequences of global warming. Once leaders realize the impact of climate change, they ought to act in a concerted way to reduce the risks of increased inequality.
Your opinion should be heard! Would you be so kind as to complete our online survey? Would you send us a message with your point of view? We will feature your ideas in our next article.
